function.mechanism: Acts as an inert mineral flow aid (reducing powder caking) and as a white pigment/opacifier in authorized color uses.
common_food_categories: Soft and hard candies and mints
Powdered foods where anticaking function is needed

adi.basis: No numerical ADI required for calcium carbonate itself in EFSA follow-up; impurity specifications (notably aluminium) remain a concern.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern for calcium carbonate per se at reported uses (including infants <16 weeks), but raised concern about unavoidable aluminium impurity and recommended specification updates.

adi.basis: NOT LIMITED (JECFA), with consideration of total dietary calcium load.

concerns.summary: Regulatory concern is centered on unavoidable aluminium impurity in E170 specifications rather than intrinsic toxicity of calcium carbonate.

Calcium supplement literature is mixed: one meta-analysis reported increased CVD risk in postmenopausal women, while a later meta-analysis of randomized trials did not find significant excess CHD/stroke risk.
High total calcium intake from multiple sources (diet plus supplementation/fortification) can approach or exceed nutritional upper levels in some populations, even if additive-only exposure is lower.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2023 found no safety concern for calcium carbonate per se at currently reported uses and use levels, including infants below 16 weeks.
JECFA ADI is NOT LIMITED for calcium carbonate.
US FDA framework lists calcium carbonate under direct food substances affirmed as GRAS (21 CFR Part 184, section 184.1191).

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is set by EFSA/JECFA for calcium carbonate itself; risk management focuses on total calcium load and additive impurities.

risk_assessment.rationale: Core toxicology and regulatory reviews indicate low concern for calcium carbonate itself at authorized uses, but practical caveats remain for impurity control (aluminium) and cumulative calcium exposure from multiple sources.
key_factors: EFSA: no numerical ADI needed and no concern for calcium carbonate per se at reported uses
FDA GRAS listing under 21 CFR 184.1191 with cGMP condition
No IARC classification found for calcium carbonate
Residual uncertainty from impurity concerns and mixed high-dose supplement cardiovascular literature
